purpose: Test whether the existing six-dimensional magnetic response supports its uniform-polarization preparation when spatial polarization textures are admitted.
status: Frozen before computing texture Hessians or nonlinear texture energies
polarization: Unit four-component positive-band chiral spinor z(x); reference z0=(1,0,0,0)
kernel: P_k M=P_k*M+M*P_k with P_k=k*k^T/|k|^2 for nonzero k on R^6
energy: tau*integral n*|gradient z|^2 - kappa/2*integral |P_k Fourier[n J(z)]|^2 dk/(2*pi)^6
coefficients: tau=1/(2*m), g=e/(2*m), kappa=g^2/Z; hbar=1; no added restoring interaction
parameter_scope: Inherited illustrative Dirac-Maxwell benchmark, not measured six-dimensional electron parameters
texture_family: z=cos(epsilon*f(x))*z0 + sin(epsilon*f(x))*v, v any normalized ray-orthogonal complex spinor; f=sin(q*x0) or cos(q*x0)
reference_prediction_under_test: The inherited benchmark is stationary and has no negative energy curvature in the specified texture family
stronger_claim_under_test: Uniform polarization remains a local minimum throughout the predeclared positive-coupling stress cases

failure_rules.nonlinear_negative_witness: A refined direct texture energy below the uniform reference confirms failure for that prepared state

interpretation: A failed preparation does not refute spatial depth six. Survival is only for this perturbation family and does not prove full field or molecular stability.
exclusions: changing the kernel after a failure
retuning the reference parameters after seeing results
adding compensating vector or scalar channels
identifying polarization fields with particle orbits
